API-07.evidence: Scheduled scans have serialized concurrency, a timeout, GitHub failure notification, scan-level persisted status/metrics/error codes, per-source health, and a production-triggered end-to-end run.

API-08.evidence: FastAPI emits an OpenAPI contract for JSON routes, but no contract-conformance or breaking-change gate exists.

API-09.evidence: Web queries clamp scores and repository reads use fixed maximum limits; sorting is static and not constructed from user input.

AUTH-01.evidence: Production authentication is delegated to native Supabase Auth. Live Adam and SysAd password sign-ins succeeded and resolved to server-managed account records.

AUTH-02.evidence: The default-deny Supabase middleware wraps every route except login, health, readiness, and static assets. A live anonymous request redirected to /login.

AUTH-03.evidence: Signed browser sessions expire after seven days and refresh Supabase tokens near expiry, but a live captured-cookie replay still returned 200 after logout. Immediate logout invalidation is broken.

AUTH-04.evidence: The production signed session cookie was observed with Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, and a seven-day maximum age. It does not use the __Host- prefix.

AUTH-05.evidence: Supabase Auth provides managed reset and verification token machinery, but Ferminator exposes no reset flow and no single-use, expiry, enumeration, or session-invalidation test was run.

AUTH-06.evidence: Login has a five-attempt/five-minute in-memory per-client limiter with generic errors. It is not per-account, not shared across instances, and reset/signup/OTP flows are not covered.

AUTH-07.evidence: Admin onboarding enforces a 12-character minimum. The live Supabase advisor reports leaked-password protection is disabled, and no stronger length or breach-list policy was verified.

AUTH-08.evidence: No MFA or passkey is configured; the SysAd beta account authenticates with password only. This is a documented beta deferral, not an N/A control.

AUTH-09.evidence: No OAuth/OIDC flow exists in the current application.

AUTH-10.evidence: Supabase validates tokens at issuance and refresh, but ordinary Ferminator requests trust the signed application cookie's user_id without validating the access token or provider session. Live post-logout replay succeeded.

AUTH-11.evidence: Cascade deletion behavior is documented and represented in migrations, but no user-facing access/export/deletion workflow or end-to-end deletion artifact exists.

AUTH-12.evidence: Administrative account provisioning writes an actor, target, action, request ID, and before/after state to public.admin_audit_events. The server database role can still mutate or delete the table, so append-only enforcement is incomplete.

AUTHZ-01.evidence: Each authenticated user resolves to a server-managed account and profile, and repository calls use that profile slug. Production role tests passed, but no hosted User A/User B resource-substitution matrix exists.

AUTHZ-02.evidence: Production has RLS on all public tables and auth.uid()-based ownership policies on profile data. The application still uses a privileged direct database credential, so RLS does not backstop a missing server repository predicate; no hosted two-user drill exists.

AUTHZ-03.evidence: Role is loaded server-side from public.accounts. Live Adam access to /admin returned 403; live SysAd access returned 200 and SysAd user-page access redirected to /admin.

AUTHZ-04.evidence: The native-auth roles, account/profile binding, server-only admin control plane, direct-client RLS policy, and deliberate beta exceptions are documented and match the deployed code.
